- No reproducible symptom exacerbation with dairy, fatty, or high-fiber foods — reduces likelihood of lactose intolerance, bile acid malabsorption, or food-driven microscopic colitis.  
- All key objective tests (fecal calprotectin, stool studies, tTG-IgA) are pending — no evidence yet of inflammation, infection, or celiac disease.

- Fecal calprotectin result — essential to rule out mucosal inflammation (IBD, microscopic colitis).

- Serum tTG-IgA level — needed to exclude celiac disease, especially given chronic diarrhea (though dietary gluten exposure must be confirmed for test validity).  
- Colonoscopy with biopsies — gold standard to diagnose microscopic colitis or quiescent IBD, but not yet performed.  
- Detailed dietary history (e.g., gluten intake adequacy pre-tTG, caffeine, artificial sweeteners) — may refine functional vs. dietary triggers.

[DIAGNOSIS]  
Irritable bowel syndrome, diarrhea-predominant (IBS-D)

**Initial Differential Diagnosis Includes:**

- Infectious colitis (persistent or recurrent) — requires exclusion via stool testing.  
- Celiac disease — must be ruled out serologically (and with appropriate dietary context).  
- Irritable bowel syndrome (IBS-D) — less likely given mucus and duration, but remains possible if objective inflammation/infection is excluded.
